children: The AIB Ireland Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.4 in August 2026 from 55.1 in July, marking its highest reading in three months.

New orders expanded at their fastest pace in nearly four and a half years, supporting a sharp increase in output, which grew for the tenth consecutive month and at its strongest pace since April 2025.
Employment also rose for a ninth consecutive month, although growth eased from July’s multi-year high.
Purchasing activity remained solid, while firms continued building inventories as supply-chain delays persisted.
Export demand remained subdued due to the Middle East conflict, while transportation delays and capacity constraints extended supplier lead times and pushed backlogs higher.
Input cost inflation accelerated, driven by higher energy and raw material prices, although output price inflation eased to a five-month low.
Business confidence strengthened to its highest since January, with around half of manufacturers expecting higher output over the next year.

title: Ireland Factory Growth Hits 3-Month High
